name: MonarchWeeklyHoursEditor
title: WeeklyHoursEditor
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of days, each a MonarchSwitchRow (androidx.compose.material3.Switch) with pairs of MonarchSelect (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox) for the start and end times
summary: Edits weekly availability: each day switched on or off, one or more time intervals per day, copying a day to the whole week, and overlap checks.
whenToUse: Booking availability, business hours, support or on-call hours: any setting that is “these times on these weekdays”.
whenNotToUse: For one-off dates such as holidays or time off, use a date list with the Material 3 DatePicker (date-picker). For rotas that change week to week, use MonarchShiftRoster.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchWeeklyHoursEditor(value: List<MonarchWeeklyHoursInterval>, onValueChange: (List<MonarchWeeklyHoursInterval>) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null, is24Hour: Boolean? = null, step: Int = 15, defaultStart: Int = 540, defaultEnd: Int = 1020, maxIntervals: Int = 6, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, timeZoneLabel: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchWeeklyHoursEditorLabels = MonarchWeeklyHoursEditorLabels())
public data class MonarchWeeklyHoursInterval(day: Int, start: Int, end: Int) { companion object { fun validate(value: List<MonarchWeeklyHoursInterval>): Map<Int, MonarchWeeklyHoursError> } }
public enum class MonarchWeeklyHoursError { Range, Order, Overlap }

public class MonarchWeeklyHoursEditorLabels(title: String? = null, unavailable: String? = null, start: String? = null, end: String? = null, add: String? = null, addItem: ((day: String) -> String)? = null, remove: String? = null, removeItem: ((day: String, position: Int) -> String)? = null, copyToAll: String? = null, copyToAllItem: ((day: String) -> String)? = null, copied: ((day: String) -> String)? = null, range: ((start: String, end: String) -> String)? = null, midnight: String? = null, rangeError: String? = null, orderError: String? = null, overlapError: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The intervals: ISO weekday (1 Monday … 7 Sunday) and minutes from midnight, end exclusive and at most 1440.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new value after every change, ordered by weekday; each day's intervals stay in the order arranged.

options.name: firstDayOfWeek
options.description: The first day shown, Calendar.SUNDAY to Calendar.SATURDAY. null follows the locale (Monday in Germany, Sunday in the US), as the system calendar does.

options.name: is24Hour
options.description: Shows times on a 24-hour clock; null follows the device setting.

options.name: step
options.description: Minutes between time options, 1 to 60; zero or a negative step falls back to 15.

options.name: defaultStart
options.description: The start of a day switched on for the first time (09:00).

options.name: defaultEnd
options.description: The end of a day switched on for the first time (17:00).

options.name: maxIntervals
options.description: The most intervals per day; the add button is hidden at this count.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the hours can be changed.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Shows each day's hours as text, without controls.

options.name: timeZoneLabel
options.description: Content under the heading for the zone the hours are in: a text, or the app's MonarchTimezoneSelect.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each remove button; without it the button reads Remove.

states.name: day on
states.description: The switch is on; each interval shows its start and end menus and a remove button; Add interval and Copy to all follow.

states.name: day off
states.description: The switch is off and the row reads Unavailable in the muted color.

states.name: invalid
states.description: A danger-coloured message under the day says what is wrong: a time outside the day, an interval ending before it starts, or an overlap.

states.name: at the limit
states.description: With maxIntervals intervals the add button is hidden.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Each day is its name and its hours as text, such as 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM, without controls.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every switch, menu and button is disabled.

appearance: Days are separated by subtle dividers. The day switch is the Material 3 Switch in Monarch colors; the time menus are outlined fields with the input border; the buttons are small ghost MonarchButtons; Unavailable and the read-only hours use the muted text color and errors the strong danger text color. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the color roles.
platformNotes: Same value shape, validation and defaults as the web, except the first day of the week (`{ day, start, end }` in minutes, ISO weekdays, 09:00 to 17:00, 15-minute steps, six intervals). Differences: firstDayOfWeek takes the java.util.Calendar constants that MonarchMiniMonth and MonarchCalendarMonthView use and, like them, follows the locale when null where the web starts on Monday; and is24Hour replaces the web's hourCycle; onValueChange passes only the value, and MonarchWeeklyHoursInterval.validate gives the errors the web passes beside it. On a phone the start and end menus share one line and the remove button sits under them, with Add interval and Copy to all under the day, instead of the web's one-line row. Times are Monarch menus, not the Material 3 TimePicker, because the TimePicker has no step and no end-of-day 24:00. The menus have the visible labels Start and End; TalkBack reads them inside the day's group after the day switch, where the web uses hidden names such as “Monday interval 1 start”. The web's hidden form input (name) has no meaning in Compose. iOS names the first day firstWeekday.
accessibility: Each day is a switch named by the weekday, with Unavailable read as its description while off; the whole row is the 48dp target.
Each day is a traversal group, so its switch, menus, buttons and error are read together.
Remove, Add interval and Copy to all carry names with the day, such as “Remove Monday interval 1” and “Copy to all days from Monday”, and keep the visible text in the name.
A day's error is text, not only color, and is announced through a polite live region when it appears.
Copying a day is announced through a polite live region (“Monday hours copied to every day.”).
The heading is a heading; the read-only view merges each day's name and hours into one element.
edgeCases: Switching a day off and on again restores its intervals while the editor stays on screen; it starts from the default interval after the editor leaves the composition.
A stored time that is not on the step is kept and offered in the menu.
Intervals with a day outside 1 to 7 are dropped at the next change.
The end of the day is Midnight on a 12-hour clock and 24:00 on a 24-hour clock.
The editor does not scroll on its own: put it in a scrolling screen.
